name: Nobara Linux
summary: An independent, modified Linux distribution based on Fedora Linux, created by Thomas Crider (GloriousEggroll) and optimized for PC gaming, streaming, and multimedia content creation. Nobara is not an official Fedora spin; it overlays Fedora's core package repositories with custom Nobara repositories, a custom Linux kernel (kernel-nobara) incorporating Zen/Liquorix and Fsync patches, Mesa drivers with enabled hardware video codecs, automated NVIDIA GPU driver configuration, pre-integrated Steam and Proton-GE, OBS Studio with Wayland capture, the Calamares installer configuring Btrfs Timeshift subvolumes, and a permissive SELinux configuration.
license: GPL-2.0-or-later, MIT, and redistributable upstream and third-party RPM licenses

content.introduction: Nobara Linux is an independent desktop Linux distribution engineered to provide an out-of-the-box computing environment tailored specifically for video gaming, live streaming, and multimedia content production. Founded in 2022 by Thomas Crider—a Red Hat software maintenance engineer widely recognized in the open-source gaming community under the pseudonym GloriousEggroll (author of Proton-GE and Wine-GE)—Nobara addresses the friction points commonly encountered on mainstream Linux distributions regarding proprietary hardware drivers, video codecs, anti-cheat compatibility, and gaming latency.
content.what_is_it: Technically, Nobara Linux is an independent downstream derivative based on the Fedora Linux package ecosystem. It combines Fedora's stable core libraries and GNU toolchain with custom-built package repositories (`nobara-baseos`, `nobara-appstream`, `nobara-rocm-official`), an extensively patched Linux kernel (`kernel-nobara`), patched Mesa graphics drivers with restored hardware codec support, the Calamares system installer, a preconfigured Btrfs snapshot layout, and dedicated graphical system maintenance utilities.
content.origin_and_history: Thomas Crider established Nobara Linux in 2022 to streamline desktop Linux setup for gamers and content creators who appreciated Fedora's package currency and stability but struggled with manual configuration of RPM Fusion, proprietary NVIDIA drivers, multimedia codecs, and Wine dependencies. Initially built with a customized GNOME desktop in Nobara 36, the project replaced Fedora's Anaconda installer with Calamares in December 2022. Beginning with Nobara 39 in late 2023, the project shifted its flagship 'Official Edition' to KDE Plasma to better support Wayland fractional scaling, variable refresh rate (VRR), and HDR. Subsequent releases, including Nobara 40 (July 2024), Nobara 41, 42, and the 44 series, unified installation images for AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA hardware.
content.governance_and_organization: Nobara Linux is maintained as an open-source community hobby project led by Thomas Crider with international volunteer contributors. Source code for package modifications, kernel patches, and build scripts is publicly hosted on GitHub under the `Nobara-Project` organization. The project is non-commercial and financed through community micro-donations via Ko-fi to support mirror bandwidth and build infrastructure.
content.relationship_with_fedora: Nobara Linux maintains a clear and documented boundary with Fedora: it is explicitly **not** an official Fedora spin, nor is it endorsed, affiliated with, or supported by Red Hat or the Fedora Project. Nobara uses Fedora's binary packages and DNF repository infrastructure as a base, but modifies packages, kernel flags, and security policies in ways that depart from Fedora's strict legal guidelines regarding patent-encumbered codecs and third-party proprietary drivers.
content.calamares_installer_and_btrfs: Nobara replaced Fedora's Anaconda installer with the universal Calamares installer. Calamares partitions storage drives using the Btrfs filesystem by default, automatically generating separated `@` (root) and `@home` (user files) subvolumes. This layout enables seamless integration with Timeshift, permitting instant system snapshot creation and restoration without risking personal user data.
content.privacy_and_telemetry: Nobara Linux enforces an open-source privacy model. It contains no commercial advertising, device fingerprinting, or user behavioral tracking. Network communications are restricted to user-directed package downloads, automated repository metadata refreshes via `nobara-updater`, and NTP clock synchronization.
advantages: Gaming-optimized Fedora derivative eliminating manual codec, driver, and Wine configuration hurdles
Custom kernel-nobara integrating Fsync and Zen scheduling patches for reduced gaming stutter
Mesa drivers compiled with full hardware video acceleration (H.264/H.265) enabled out of the box
Calamares installer configuring Btrfs with dedicated @ and @home subvolumes for Timeshift snapshots
Native integration of Proton-GE, MangoHud, OBS Studio, and handheld device controller profiles
Dedicated Update System utility preventing broken package dependencies during repository upgrades
disadvantages: SELinux configured in Permissive mode by default, reducing enterprise security hardening compared to Fedora
Requires disabling UEFI Secure Boot in motherboard firmware due to unsigned custom kernel modules
Hobby community project without official corporate support or formal enterprise SLAs
Software updates may be temporarily held back while waiting for upstream graphics stack stabilization
Exclusive support for 64-bit x86_64, with no official ARM builds for single-board computers
content.who_is_it_for: Nobara Linux is designed for PC gamers, live streamers, content creators, and handheld PC enthusiasts who want the modern package currency and stability of Fedora combined with preconfigured gaming drivers, low-latency kernels, and multimedia codecs without manual terminal tweaking.
content.who_is_it_not_for: It is not intended for mission-critical enterprise servers requiring strict SELinux enforcement, corporate workstations mandating UEFI Secure Boot compliance, or users seeking a pure, unmodified upstream Fedora experience.

components.name: kernel-nobara
components.note: Custom-compiled Linux kernel with Fsync, Zen low-latency scheduling, and hardware controller patches.

components.name: Mesa (Freeworld)
components.note: Mesa 3D graphics drivers compiled with hardware-accelerated H.264/H.265 VA-API codecs enabled.

components.name: Calamares Installer
components.note: Independent system installer replacing Anaconda and configuring Btrfs subvolume layouts.

components.name: Update System (nobara-updater)
components.note: Specialized update utility coordinating RPM, Flatpak, and repository GPG key synchronizations.

components.name: Nobara Welcome
components.note: First-boot graphical setup wizard for driver configuration, codecs, and gaming utilities.

components.name: Steam & Proton-GE
components.note: Gaming runtime environment bundling 32-bit libraries, Proton-GE, and Wine-GE layers.

components.name: OBS Studio (Nobara Build)
components.note: Video recording and broadcasting suite configured with Wayland PipeWire capture and NVENC plugins.

components.name: Gamescope
components.note: Micro-compositor developed by Valve enabling resolution scaling and isolated display containers.

components.name: MangoHud & GOverlay
components.note: On-screen display layer for real-time monitoring of gaming frame rates, thermals, and power.

relations.name: Fedora
relations.note: Base distribution providing underlying binary packages, GNU toolchain, and RPM repository infrastructure.

relations.name: Arch Linux
relations.note: Peer enthusiast distribution frequently utilized for gaming and cutting-edge kernel deployments.

relations.name: Pop!_OS
relations.note: Peer distribution featuring gaming-focused defaults and out-of-the-box proprietary graphics support.
